note: Maps each vendored WPT directory to a scope bucket. Seeded from docs/web-api-priorities.md's coverage map. in-scope: run, count toward conformance. partial: run, but most failures are runner limits (server handlers / multi-origin / iframes) excluded from the denominator. stub-only: run, but genuine conformance failures are out-of-scope-by-design. out-of-scope dirs are never vendored or walked. See docs/decisions/0016-wpt-conformance.md.

rules.note: pragmatic parser; WHATWG edge cases fail by design
no real backpressure; byte-streams fail by design
no-op console: existence passes, output-assertions fail by design
in-memory stub; conformance failures are out-of-scope-by-design

harness_limited_note: These suites assert on the headers a SERVER RECEIVED (Sec-Fetch-*, Referer) via wptserve .py echo handlers. unblink SENDS spec-correct Sec-Fetch and Referrer headers (ADR 0013), but a single-process client-side harness has no server to observe receipt, so the suites are not measurable here — counted as (d) harness-limited with one descriptor per test rather than run (they would otherwise 404 the .py echo and time out en masse).
by_design_note: Two families are counted as out-of-scope-by-design rather than run. (1) Legacy (non-UTF-8) encoding conformance — TextDecoder is UTF-8-first; these are also form/iframe-based and variant-exploded, so running them adds cost not signal. (2) CSP directives unblink deliberately does not enforce (ADR 0014): the resource-type directives (img/style/font/media/frame/child/object-src) it never gates because it only loads scripts, the document directives (base-uri/form-action/frame-ancestors/sandbox/plugin-types), and the reporting surface. unblink enforces script-src(+attr-elem)/connect-src/default-src + nonce/hash/strict-dynamic/unsafe-eval, so those directive subtrees ARE run for real signal.
